sourceEvidence.quote:
IgA protease
Enzyme that cleaves IgA, allowing bacteria to adhere to and colonize mucous membranes. Secreted
by S pneumoniae, H influenzae type b, and Neisseria (SHiN).

sourceEvidence.claim: M protein row (full physical order; molecular mimicry)
sourceEvidence.quote:
M protein
Helps prevent phagocytosis. Expressed by group A streptococci. Sequence homology with human
cardiac myosin (molecular mimicry); possibly underlies the autoimmune response seen in acute
rheumatic fever.

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source facts.

kypExtensions.summary: The drug-journey model of resistance (a drug must accumulate, stay intact, and fit its target — each mechanism class removes one leg); the immune-evasion arsenal as four pressures defeated (phagocytosis/complement, opsonization, mucosal IgA, phagocytosis+mimicry); the Protein A backwards-IgG explanation; the mimicry-to-autoimmunity chain (cardiac myosin homology → acute rheumatic fever carditis); and the cleavage-list vs target-list split at the β-lactamase line — with post-strep glomerulonephritis and altered-PBP/MRSA notes labeled as extensions.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the figure without the drug-journey taxonomy or the mimicry-autoimmunity chain; these integrations are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanism captions + callout + patterns + mnemonics + miniCase
